item.title: Haze smoke experienced in Port Moresby
item.description: Hazy smoke has been evident in the skies of Port Moresby for past days. The National Weather Service has explained that the smoky appearance maybe caused by smoke, airborne particles or weather conditions, which are slow in dispersing.
item.content:encoded:
Hazy smoke has been evident in the skies of Port Moresby for past days.

The National Weather Service has explained that the smoky appearance maybe caused by smoke, airborne particles or weather conditions, which are slow in dispersing.

At this time of the year, the Weather Service also noted that Port Moresby is usually affected by dry southeasterly winds which can limit the amount of moisture available for rainfall.

The National Weather Service is yet to confirm the exact cause of the haze smoke being experienced in Port Moresby.

It indicated that the smoky appearance maybe caused by smoke, airborne particles or weather conditions, which are slow in dispersing.

The office noted that haze is heavy during the morning hours when very small particles float in the air and make it difficult to see clearly over long distances.

And, this comes especially from burning grass, bushfires, rubbish, dust from roads among others.

Haze can be harmful to people’s health and therefore the weather office is encouraging people to take precautionary measures like wearing face masks or stay indoors.

Meantime, in a separate report to the National Newspaper, the Weather Service Assistant Director Kasis Inape says the hazy conditions could be associated with fires from Indonesia however further analysis of satellite imagery, fire locations and prevailing wind patterns is required to establish its actual origin.

item.title: Bush fire threatens Lou Island villages in Manus
item.description: A bushfire that has been burning for more than a week on Lou Island in Manus Province is threatening nearby villages, a health centre and food gardens, prompting an urgent appeal for firefighting assistance. According to information provided by local residents, many food gardens have been affected by the blaze, raising concerns about livelihoods and food security.
item.content:encoded:
A bushfire that has been burning for more than a week on Lou Island in Manus Province is threatening nearby villages, a health centre and food gardens, prompting an urgent appeal for firefighting assistance.

According to information provided by local residents, many food gardens have been affected by the blaze, raising concerns about livelihoods and food security.

The situation comes amid the current El Niño period in Papua New Guinea, with dry conditions already affecting food gardens and water supplies on Lou Island. The ongoing bushfire has placed additional pressure on local food production, raising concerns about food security and the livelihoods of households that depend on locally grown produce for their daily needs.

The fire is reportedly close to Lako Village and the health centre, which also serves as the LLG administrative centre. Rei Village is also reported to be in the path of the advancing fire.

The cause of the fire remains unknown. Reports of possible injuries among people involved in firefighting efforts have not been confirmed, while the full extent of the damage is yet to be established.

Local authorities and the Provincial Disaster Office have reportedly been informed of the situation.

The affected community is appealing for urgent assistance, including firefighting personnel, high-volume water pumps and technical support to assess the fire’s boundaries and establish containment lines.

The community is also requesting helicopter support equipped with a monsoon bucket system to deliver water directly onto active sections of the fire and help contain its spread.

Efforts have reportedly been made to seek assistance from Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), the Australian Defence Force and Pacific Helicopters.

The community is urging relevant authorities to coordinate an urgent response to limit further damage and protect nearby villages, food gardens and essential facilities.

The situation remains concerning as residents await further assistance.

item.title: Maprik MP Libert Kapris passes on
item.description: The death of Maprik MP Libert Kapris has been confirmed, sending shockwaves through East Sepik Province and the wider Sepik region. East Sepik Governor Allan Bird confirmed the tragic news in a media statement, saying he had received confirmation from the Deputy Clerk of Parliament.
item.content:encoded:
The death of Maprik MP Libert Kapris has been confirmed, sending shockwaves through East Sepik Province and the wider Sepik region.

East Sepik Governor Allan Bird confirmed the tragic news in a media statement, saying he had received confirmation from the Deputy Clerk of Parliament.

Kapris died this morning at PIH in Port Moresby with the cause of death yet to be established, and no further details surrounding the circumstances of his death have been officially released.

Governor Bird described the news as tragic and deeply saddening, saying the Kapris family had suffered significant loss in a short period.

He appealed to the people of Maprik to remain calm during the period of mourning and allow the appropriate arrangements involving Parliament and the family to proceed.

The East Sepik Provincial Government will work closely with the Kapris family and Parliament as funeral arrangements are prepared.

Governor Bird also extended condolences on behalf of the people of the Greater Sepik Region to the Kapris family and their relatives.

Kapris won the Maprik Open by-election in June 2024, representing the People’s First Party, succeeding his father late Gabriel Kapris as Maprik MP.

Further official information regarding the circumstances of his death and funeral arrangements is expected to be released later.

item.title: Relief supplies reach North Fly as dry spell worsens
item.description: Families in remote areas of North Fly District in Western Province cut off by falling river levels are set to receive essential food and water supplies, after the first consignment of humanitarian relief landed in Tabubil yesterday. The supplies, flown in from Port Moresby, mark the beginning of a coordinated humanitarian relief operation involving air, sea and river transport to reach villages wh
item.content:encoded:
Families in remote areas of North Fly District in Western Province cut off by falling river levels are set to receive essential food and water supplies, after the first consignment of humanitarian relief landed in Tabubil yesterday.

The supplies, flown in from Port Moresby, mark the beginning of a coordinated humanitarian relief operation involving air, sea and river transport to reach villages where gardens have failed and water sources are drying up.

Western Province has been one of the hardest hits by the prolonged dry spell, with communities reporting critical shortages.

Today's flight, operated by the Royal Australian Air Force, is the first of four planned sorties. The initial load of two tons will help the disaster response team on the ground finalize distribution plans.

More bulk supplies are being mobilized by barge. At Port Moresby's Kennedy and Oyster Bay ports, a combined 240 tons of humanitarian relief supplies are being dispatched for shipment to Tabubil and Aiambak - from where they will be moved upriver to affected communities.

The humanitarian operation is being coordinated by the North Fly Disaster Response Team together with the Papua New Guinea Sustainable Development Program and Ok Tedi Mining Limited, who have come on board to support the humanitarian response.

Officials coordinating the relief operation say further distribution of relief assistance will continue in phases as access routes are confirmed.

item.content:encoded:
Hela Provincial Police Commander (PPC), Inspector Arau Mairi has confirmed that police have arrested the male student who allegedly attacked a Grade 12 examination invigilator at Komo Secondary School in Komo-Hulia District on Wednesday, 14th October 2026 at approximately 9:15am.

PPC Mairi said the suspect is now being held at the Tari Police Station cell. He said the matter has been handed over to the Police Criminal Investigation Division (CID) for processing, with formal charges to follow. The suspect is from Apono village in the Hayapuga Local Level Government (LLG) of Hela Province.

He said the victim, Virgil Verave, a teacher attached to the Catholic Archdiocese Education Division, was deployed to the school - a Catholic Agency-run school - to invigilate the ongoing Grade 12 National Examinations when he was attacked.

He said during the examination, Mr. Verave allegedly discovered students cheating by offering cash bribes in exchange for examination answers.

"When the cheating was exposed, a student (name withheld) who is the current SRC President of the school allegedly took a bush knife, chased the teacher out of the classroom onto the school grounds, and slashed him on the head, hands, and calf muscles," PPC Mairi said.

He said Mr. Verave, who is from Gabone village in Rigo District, Central Province, sustained serious injuries and was rushed to Tari Hospital for urgent medical attention. His condition is currently being monitored.

"I strongly condemn this attack. Teachers and examination invigilators are performing a national duty to protect the integrity of our education system. Any attack on them is an attack on the future of our children and will not be tolerated," PPC Mairi said.

item.title: Morobe entrepreneurs complete US-funded business training
item.description: Sixty-two entrepreneurs in Morobe have completed a United States-funded business training program aimed at helping small businesses improve their operations and reach new markets. The graduates received their certificates on October 15 at the Lae SME Incubator Hub at Okari Campus, following the DreamBuilder Morobe Project delivered with implementing partner Tok Stret Consulting Ltd.
item.content:encoded:
Sixty-two entrepreneurs in Morobe have completed a United States-funded business training program aimed at helping small businesses improve their operations and reach new markets.

The graduates received their certificates on October 15 at the Lae SME Incubator Hub at Okari Campus, following the DreamBuilder Morobe Project delivered with implementing partner Tok Stret Consulting Ltd.

US Embassy Port Moresby Public Affairs Officer Sarah Sanderson said the program was designed to help entrepreneurs build businesses that could compete and grow.

“The United States believes the best path to lasting prosperity is trade, not aid,” Sanderson said.

“We're here to help build real businesses that compete, grow, and connect to markets in Papua New Guinea, across the Pacific, and beyond.”

The graduates operate businesses in distribution, automotive services, agriculture, construction, transport and retail.

Through the DreamBuilder online learning platform, participants gained skills in bookkeeping, maintaining a reliable supply of goods, quality control and building strong customer relationships.

The program was established in 2019 and uses a free online platform developed by Arizona State University's Thunderbird School of Global Management and the Freeport-McMoRan Foundation.

Sanderson said Morobe businesses had already demonstrated their ability to reach international markets.

She cited Muruk Tropical Produce Limited, which shipped frozen taro from Morobe to California in 2023. The taro was sourced from farmers in Lae, Nawaeb, Markham, Huon Gulf and Finschhafen districts.

She also pointed to Kongo Coffee Limited, a specialty Arabica coffee business with a branch in Lae, which has exported coffee to buyers in the United States.

Sanderson said growing Papua New Guinean businesses could create opportunities for companies in both countries.

“When Papua New Guinean businesses grow, American companies gain reliable suppliers and trusted partners, and both our nations grow more prosperous,” she said.

She urged the graduates to apply their new skills, develop relationships with buyers and mentor other aspiring entrepreneurs in Morobe.

The program aims to help small businesses strengthen their operations and build connections with markets in Papua New Guinea and overseas.

item.title: Work on new Numuru bridge in Madang progressing well
item.description: Construction work on the new Numuru bridge is progressing well, according to the Department of Works and Highways in Madang. Construction workers began launching the new bridge across the river on Wednesday after successfully assembling it early this week.
item.content:encoded:
Construction work on the new Numuru bridge is progressing well, according to the Department of Works and Highways in Madang.

Construction workers began launching the new bridge across the river on Wednesday after successfully assembling it early this week.

They completed the process yesterday morning and have moved onto the next phase of installing decks and then, work on the footings.

The Numuru bridge collapsed last month under a heavy load of gravel that was on route to Bogia for similar civil works.

The bridge is likely to be ready for use in a week's time.

NBC News was on site yesterday and witnessed the completion of the bridge launching.

Locals we spoke to expressed gratitude to the government and the Department of Works and Highways for fast- tracking the construction of the new bridge.

Commuters are currently still using a bamboo footbridge and boats to cross over the river at a fee of K2.00 per person whilst charges for cargoes vary, depending on the loads.

Buai buyers and sellers are equally happy with the progress of reconstruction, stating the past weeks have been challenging for them as they continue to pay K10 for a bag of betelnut to be ferried across the river.

Meanwhile, wet- crossing on the beach front is no longer possible as it trespasses a conservation area, and locals were charging a hundred kina per vehicle.

item.title: Grade 12 exam disrupted by armed intruders in Wewak
item.description: Grade 12 examinations at Bishop Leo secondary school in Wewak were disrupted today after a group of intruders allegedly entered an examination room and attacked students and invigilators. NBC News was reliably informed by school staff that the security breach occurred while Grade 12 students were sitting for their Mathematics Examination Paper 2.
item.content:encoded:
Grade 12 examinations at Bishop Leo secondary school in Wewak were disrupted today after a group of intruders allegedly entered an examination room and attacked students and invigilators.

NBC News was reliably informed by school staff that the security breach occurred while Grade 12 students were sitting for their Mathematics Examination Paper 2.

According to the information received, the intruders were allegedly armed with guns and wire catapults and damaged examination papers during the incident.

One male student was reportedly injured after being struck by a projectile from a wire catapult and was taken to Boram hospital for medical attention.

Police are now on the ground assessing the situation.

Following the incident, students have protested to the Provincial Education Division over the security breach, while police continue to monitor the situation.

Further details are expected as authorities establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

item.title: Lae businesses still struggle with power blackouts
item.description: The commissioning of a new transmission line is a step towards improving electricity reliability in Lae, but businesses and residents continue to face prolonged blackouts and rising operating costs.

item.title: NDC supports North Fly drought response
item.description: Member for North Fly James Donald has thanked the National Disaster Centre for its timely support in coordinating logistics and hiring a landing craft to freight 120 tons of food relief supplies to affected communities in North Fly District of Western Province.
